title.zh: 卷五十一 志第四十一 食貨一
title.raw: 卷五十一 志第四十一 食貨一 Volume 51 Treatises 47: Finance and Economics 1

sentences.zh: 食貨一

translations.literal: Food and Commodities, Part 1
translations.idiomatic: Finance and Economics, Part 1

sentences.zh: 古之善治其國而愛養斯民者，必立經常簡易之法，使上愛物以養其下，下勉力以事其上，上足而下不困。

translations.literal: In antiquity, those who governed their states well and lovingly nourished the people always established regular and simple laws, causing superiors to cherish goods to nourish those below and those below to strive with effort to serve those above—superiors had sufficiency and those below were not distressed.
translations.idiomatic: In ancient times, rulers who governed well and cared for their people always set up steady, straightforward institutions, so that the court valued resources to support the common folk while the people worked diligently to serve the throne—enough for the state above and no hardship among the people below.

sentences.zh: 故量人之力而授之田，量地之產而取以給公上，量其入而出之以為用度之數。

translations.literal: Therefore they measured men's strength to grant them fields, measured the land's yield to take for supplying the public above, and measured income to disburse it as the reckoning of expenditure.
translations.idiomatic: They matched each person's capacity when allotting farmland, took from the land's yield only what was needed for public revenue, and balanced intake against outlay to set the budget.

sentences.zh: 是三者常相須以濟而不可失，失其一則不能守其二。

translations.literal: These three constantly relied on one another to succeed and could not be lost; lose one and one could not keep the other two.
translations.idiomatic: These three principles had to work together; if any one failed, the other two could not hold.

sentences.zh: 及暴君庸主，縱其佚欲，而茍且之吏從之，變制合時以取寵於其上。

translations.literal: When it came to tyrannical rulers and mediocre lords who indulged their idle desires, opportunistic officials followed them, altering institutions to suit the moment to win favor from above.
translations.idiomatic: When tyrants and weak sovereigns gave free rein to their appetites, short-sighted officials went along, changing the rules to suit the moment and curry favor at court.

sentences.zh: 故用於上者無節，而取於下者無限，民竭其力而不能供，由是上愈不足而下愈困，則財利之說興，而聚斂之臣用。

translations.literal: Thus expenditure above had no restraint and exactions from below had no limit; the people exhausted their strength yet could not supply it, whereupon the court grew ever more insufficient and the people ever more distressed, and then doctrines of profit arose and revenue-grasping ministers were employed.
translations.idiomatic: Court spending knew no bounds while levies on the people knew no limit; the populace gave everything they had and still could not meet demand. As the treasury grew emptier and the people poorer, schemes for squeezing wealth proliferated and ministers who specialized in extraction came to power.

sentences.zh: 《記》曰：「寧畜盜臣。

translations.literal: The 《Records》 say: "Better to keep a thieving minister."
translations.idiomatic: The 《Classic of Rites》 says: "Better to tolerate a corrupt official."

sentences.zh: 」盜臣誠可惡，然一人之害爾。

translations.literal: " A thieving minister is indeed detestable, yet it is the harm of one man only.
translations.idiomatic: A corrupt official is truly abominable, but his damage falls on a single person alone.

sentences.zh: 聚斂之臣用，則經常之法壞，而下不勝其弊焉。

translations.literal: When revenue-grasping ministers are employed, the regular laws are ruined, and those below cannot bear their evils.
translations.idiomatic: When extractive ministers take charge, the standing institutions collapse, and the people cannot endure the harm.

sentences.zh: 唐之始時，授人以口分、世業田，而取之以租、庸、調之法，其用之也有節。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tang, people were granted per-capita allotment fields and hereditary estate fields, and taxes were taken by the methods of zu, yong, and diao; expenditure also had restraint.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tang dynasty was founded, the state allotted per-capita and hereditary farmland to the people and collected the grain tax, corvée levy, and textile tax under the zu-yong-diao system, while keeping spending within bounds.

sentences.zh: 蓋其畜兵以府衛之制，故兵雖多而無所損；

translations.literal: Because they maintained troops by the fubing garrison system, though soldiers were numerous there was no drain;
translations.idiomatic: Troops were raised through the fubing garrison system, so although the army was large it did not drain the realm;

sentences.zh: 設官有常員之數，故官不濫而易祿。

translations.literal: offices were established with fixed quotas, so officials were not excessive and salaries were easily met.
translations.idiomatic: and offices had fixed headcounts, so the bureaucracy did not swell and salaries remained affordable.

sentences.zh: 雖不及三代之盛時，然亦可以為經常之法也。

translations.literal: Though it did not reach the flourishing age of the Three Dynasties, it could still serve as regular law.
translations.idiomatic: It fell short of the golden ages of the Three Dynasties, yet it could still stand as a durable fiscal order.

sentences.zh: 及其弊也，兵冗官濫，為之大蠹。

translations.literal: When its abuses came, redundant troops and excessive officials became a great bane.
translations.idiomatic: When the system decayed, bloated armies and swollen bureaucracies became its gravest plague.

sentences.zh: 自天寶以來，大盜屢起，方鎮數叛，兵革之興，累世不息，而用度之數，不能節矣。

translations.literal: From the Tianbao era onward, great bandits arose repeatedly, military governors rebelled time and again, warfare continued for generations without cease, and the reckoning of expenditure could no longer be restrained.
translations.idiomatic: From the Tianbao reign onward, major rebellions broke out again and again, frontier commanders rose in repeated revolt, and war went on from one generation to the next without pause, while state spending could no longer be held in check.

sentences.zh: 加以驕君昏主，奸吏邪臣，取濟一時，屢更其制，而經常之法，蕩然盡矣。

translations.literal: Added to this were arrogant rulers and benighted sovereigns, treacherous clerks and wicked ministers who sought temporary relief, repeatedly altering the system until the regular laws were utterly swept away.
translations.idiomatic: Arrogant emperors and muddled courts, together with corrupt clerks and scheming ministers, patched over each crisis with stopgap measures, changing the rules again and again until the standing order vanished entirely.

sentences.zh: 由是財利之說興，聚斂之臣進。

translations.literal: Thereupon doctrines of profit arose and revenue-grasping ministers advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Profit-seeking policies multiplied, and ministers devoted to extraction rose to power.

sentences.zh: 蓋口分、世業之田壞而為兼並，租、庸、調之法壞而為兩稅。

translations.literal: The per-capita and hereditary estate fields were ruined and became consolidated holdings; the zu, yong, and diao methods were ruined and became the two-tax system.
translations.idiomatic: Per-capita and hereditary allotments gave way to land concentration; the zu-yong-diao taxes were replaced by the two-tax system.

sentences.zh: 至於鹽鐵、轉運、屯田、和糴、鑄錢、括苗、榷利、借商、進奉、獻助，無所不為矣。

translations.literal: As for salt and iron monopolies, transport commissions, military colonies, government grain purchases, coin minting, field surveys, state monopolies on goods, loans to merchants, tribute submissions, and voluntary contributions—there was nothing they did not do.
translations.idiomatic: Salt and iron monopolies, transport offices, military farming colonies, state grain purchases, coinage, cadastral surveys, excise monopolies, loans to merchants, tribute deliveries, and voluntary contributions to the throne—every expedient was tried.

sentences.zh: 蓋愈煩而愈弊，以至於亡焉。

translations.literal: The more tangled the measures, the worse the abuses, until the dynasty perished.
translations.idiomatic: The more elaborate the schemes grew, the deeper the rot ran, until the dynasty fell.

sentences.zh: 唐制：度田以步，其闊一步，其長二百四十步為畝，百畝為頃。

translations.literal: Tang regulations: fields were measured by paces; one pace in width and two hundred forty paces in length made one mu; one hundred mu made one qing.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang law, land was measured in paces: a field one pace wide and two hundred forty paces long counted as one mu, and one hundred mu made one qing.

sentences.zh: 凡民始生為黃，四歲為小，十六為中，二十一為丁，六十為老。

translations.literal: For the people generally, at birth one was classified huang; at four, xiao; at sixteen, zhong; at twenty-one, ding; at sixty, lao.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners were classified by age: newborns as infants, four-year-olds as children, sixteen-year-olds as youths, twenty-one-year-olds as adult males liable for service, and sixty-year-olds as elderly.

sentences.zh: 授田之制，丁及男年十八以上者，人一頃，其八十畝為口分，二十畝為永業；

translations.literal: Under the land-grant system, ding males and men eighteen years and above each received one qing; eighty mu were per-capita allotment and twenty mu were hereditary estate land;
translations.idiomatic: Under the allotment system, each adult male and every man of eighteen or older received one qing of land: eighty mu as a per-capita grant and twenty mu as a permanent holding;

sentences.zh: 老及篤疾、廢疾者，人四十畝，寡妻妾三十畝，當戶者增二十畝，皆以二十畝為永業，其余為口分。

translations.literal: the elderly and those with severe or crippling illness received forty mu each; widows and concubines thirty mu; heads of households received an additional twenty mu; in every case twenty mu were hereditary estate and the remainder per-capita allotment.
translations.idiomatic: the elderly and the severely disabled received forty mu each, widows and concubines thirty mu, and household heads an extra twenty mu; in each case twenty mu were permanent holdings and the rest per-capita allotments.

sentences.zh: 永業之田，樹以榆、棗、桑及所宜之木，皆有數。

translations.literal: On hereditary estate fields, elms, jujubes, mulberries, and trees suited to the soil were planted, each in fixed numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Permanent holdings had to be planted with prescribed numbers of elm, jujube, mulberry, and other suitable trees.

sentences.zh: 田多可以足其人者為寬鄉，少者為狹鄉。

translations.literal: Districts where fields were abundant enough to satisfy the people were called broad districts; where fields were scarce, narrow districts.
translations.idiomatic: Areas with enough land for everyone were designated broad districts; those with too little land were narrow districts.

sentences.zh: 狹鄉授田，減寬鄉之半。

translations.literal: In narrow districts land grants were reduced by half compared with broad districts.
translations.idiomatic: Narrow districts received allotments half the size of those in broad districts.

sentences.zh: 其地有薄厚，歲一易者，倍受之。

translations.literal: Where the soil was thin or fields were rotated once a year, grants were doubled.
translations.idiomatic: Where the soil was poor or fields were rotated annually, recipients received double allotments.

sentences.zh: 寬鄉三易者，不倍授。

translations.literal: In broad districts with threefold rotation, grants were not doubled.
translations.idiomatic: In broad districts with three-field rotation, no doubling was granted.

sentences.zh: 工商者，寬鄉減半，狹鄉不給。

translations.literal: For merchants and artisans, grants in broad districts were halved; in narrow districts none were given.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants and artisans received half allotments in broad districts and none in narrow districts.

sentences.zh: 凡庶人徙鄉及貧無以葬者，得賣世業田。

translations.literal: Commoners who moved districts or were too poor to bury the dead might sell hereditary estate fields.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners who moved to another district or could not afford a funeral were allowed to sell their permanent holdings.

sentences.zh: 自狹鄉而徙寬鄉者，得並賣口分田。

translations.literal: Those who moved from a narrow to a broad district might also sell per-capita allotment fields.
translations.idiomatic: Those who moved from a narrow to a broad district could sell their per-capita allotments as well.

sentences.zh: 已賣者，不復授。

translations.literal: Once sold, fields were not granted again.
translations.idiomatic: Land that had been sold was not re-allotted.

sentences.zh: 死者收之，以授無田者。

translations.literal: When the holder died, the land was taken back and granted to those without fields.
translations.idiomatic: On the holder's death, the land reverted to the state and was given to the landless.

sentences.zh: 凡收授皆以歲十月。

translations.literal: All reclamation and granting took place in the tenth month of the year.
translations.idiomatic: All reclamation and distribution of land took place in the tenth month.

sentences.zh: 授田先貧及有課役者。

translations.literal: Land was granted first to the poor and to those with tax and corvée obligations.
translations.idiomatic: Grants went first to the poor and to households liable for tax and labor service.

sentences.zh: 凡田，鄉有余以給比鄉，縣有余以給比縣，州有余以給近州。

translations.literal: For fields generally, if a district had surplus it supplied neighboring districts; if a county had surplus, neighboring counties; if a prefecture had surplus, nearby prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Surplus land in a district went to neighboring districts, surplus in a county to neighboring counties, and surplus in a prefecture to nearby prefectures.

sentences.zh: 凡授田者，丁歲輸粟二斛，稻三斛，謂之租。

translations.literal: All who received land paid each year as ding two hu of millet or three hu of rice—this was called zu.
translations.idiomatic: Every allottee paid annually, per adult male, two hu of millet or three hu of rice; this was the grain tax.

sentences.zh: 丁隨鄉所出，歲輸絹二匹，綾、絁二丈，布加五之一，綿三兩，麻三斤，非蠶鄉則輸銀十四兩，謂之調。

translations.literal: Each ding, according to what his district produced, paid yearly two bolts of silk, two zhang of ling and shi fabrics, cloth with one-fifth added, three liang of cotton, three jin of hemp; in non-sericulture districts he paid fourteen liang of silver instead—this was called diao.
translations.idiomatic: Each adult male paid yearly, according to local products, two bolts of silk, two zhang of patterned and coarse silk, cloth with an extra fifth, three liang of cotton floss, and three jin of hemp—or, in districts without sericulture, fourteen liang of silver; this was the textile tax.

sentences.zh: 用人之力，歲二十日，閏加二日，不役者日為絹三尺，謂之庸。

translations.literal: Using men's labor, twenty days per year, with two added in intercalary years; those not corvée'd paid three chi of silk per day—this was called yong.
translations.idiomatic: Labor service was twenty days a year, with two extra days in leap years; those exempt from corvée paid three chi of silk per day instead; this was the corvée levy.

sentences.zh: 有事而加役二十五日者免調，三十日者租、調皆免。

translations.literal: If special service added twenty-five days, diao was exempted; if thirty days, both zu and diao were exempted.
translations.idiomatic: If extra labor reached twenty-five days, the textile tax was waived; at thirty days, both grain and textile taxes were waived.

sentences.zh: 通正役不過五十日。

translations.literal: Regular corvée in total did not exceed fifty days.
translations.idiomatic: Regular corvée service could not exceed fifty days in all.

sentences.zh: 自王公以下，皆有永業田。

translations.literal: From kings and dukes downward, all had hereditary estate fields.
translations.idiomatic: From princes and dukes down, everyone held permanent land grants.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后、皇太后、皇后緦麻以上親，內命婦一品以上親，郡王及五品以上祖父兄弟，職事、勛官三品以上有封者若縣男父子，國子、太學、四門學生、俊士，孝子、順孫、義夫、節婦同籍者，皆免課役。

translations.literal: Relatives within mourning of the grand empress dowager, empress dowager, and empress; relatives of inner consorts of first rank and above; grandfathers and brothers of princes of the blood and officials of fifth rank and above; fathers and sons of officeholders and merit officials of third rank and above who held fiefs, such as county barons; students of the Directorate of Education, Imperial University, and Four Gates schools and distinguished scholars; filial sons, obedient grandsons, righteous husbands, and chaste widows registered in the same household—all were exempt from tax and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Kin within mourning for the grand empress dowager, empress dowager, and empress; kin of palace ladies of first rank and above; grandfathers and brothers of imperial princes and fifth-rank officials and up; fathers and sons of third-rank officeholders and merit nobles with fiefs such as county barons; students of the national academies and distinguished scholars; and filial sons, obedient grandsons, righteous husbands, and chaste widows on the same household register were all exempt from tax and labor service.

sentences.zh: 凡主戶內有課口者為課戶。

translations.literal: Among principal households, those with taxable persons were called taxable households.
translations.idiomatic: Principal households with members liable for tax were classified as taxable households.

sentences.zh: 若老及男廢疾、篤疾、寡妻妾、部曲、客女、奴婢及視九品以上官，不課。

translations.literal: The elderly, males with crippling or severe illness, widows and concubines, retainers, guest women, slaves, and those treated as officials of ninth rank and above were not taxed.
translations.idiomatic: The elderly, disabled men, the severely ill, widows and concubines, retainers, guest women, slaves, and persons ranked as ninth-rank officials or higher were not liable for tax.

sentences.zh: 凡裏有手實，歲終具民之年與地之闊狹，為鄉帳。

translations.literal: Every li had household registers; at year's end the people's ages and the breadth or narrowness of their land were compiled into district accounts.
translations.idiomatic: Each neighborhood kept household registers; at year's end ages and land holdings were compiled into district tax rolls.

sentences.zh: 鄉成於縣，縣成於州，州成於戶部。

translations.literal: Districts were consolidated at the county, counties at the prefecture, prefectures at the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: District rolls were combined at the county, county rolls at the prefecture, and prefectural rolls at the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 又有計帳，具來歲課役以報度支。

translations.literal: There were also projected accounts listing the next year's taxes and corvée to report to the Department of Public Works and Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Projected accounts also listed the coming year's taxes and labor obligations for report to the expenditure office.

sentences.zh: 國有所須，先奏而斂。

translations.literal: When the state had needs, it reported first and then levied.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the state required revenue, it sought approval before collecting.

sentences.zh: 凡稅斂之數，書於縣門、村坊，與眾知之。

translations.literal: All tax levies were written at county gates and village wards so the multitude would know.
translations.idiomatic: Tax amounts were posted at county gates and village wards for public notice.

sentences.zh: 水、旱、霜、蝗耗十四者，免其租；

translations.literal: Where flood, drought, frost, or locusts caused a loss of fourteen parts in ten, zu was remitted;
translations.idiomatic: If flood, drought, frost, or locusts destroyed fourteen-tenths of the crop, the grain tax was remitted;

sentences.zh: 桑麻盡者，免其調；

translations.literal: where mulberry and hemp were entirely lost, diao was remitted;
translations.idiomatic: if mulberry and hemp were wholly destroyed, the textile tax was remitted;

sentences.zh: 田耗十之六者，免租調；

translations.literal: where fields lost six parts in ten, zu and diao were remitted;
translations.idiomatic: if six-tenths of the fields were ruined, both grain and textile taxes were remitted;

sentences.zh: 耗七者，課、役皆免。

translations.literal: where the loss was seven parts in ten, all taxes and corvée were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: at seven-tenths loss, all taxes and labor service were waived.

sentences.zh: 凡新附之戶，春以三月免役，夏以六月免課，秋以九月課、役皆免。

translations.literal: For all newly registered households: in spring, by the third month, corvée was remitted; in summer, by the sixth month, the grain tax; in autumn, by the ninth month, both tax and corvée were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Newly registered households were exempt from corvée by the third month, from the grain tax by the sixth month, and from all taxes and service by the ninth month.

sentences.zh: 徙寬鄉者，縣覆於州，出境則覆於戶部，官以閑月達之。

translations.literal: Those who moved to broad districts were reviewed by the county and reported to the prefecture; if they crossed boundaries, review went to the Ministry of Revenue; officials transmitted reports in slack months.
translations.idiomatic: Migrants to broad districts were verified by the county and reported to the prefecture; if they crossed jurisdictional lines, the Ministry of Revenue was notified, with reports filed in off-season months.

sentences.zh: 自畿內徙畿外，自京縣徙余縣，皆有禁。

translations.literal: Moving from within the capital region to outside it, or from capital counties to other counties, was all restricted.
translations.idiomatic: Moves from the capital region to the provinces, or from metropolitan counties to other counties, were all restricted.

sentences.zh: 四夷降戶，附以寬鄉，給復十年。

translations.literal: Households of surrendered foreigners were settled in broad districts and given ten years' remission of tax and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Households of surrendered foreigners were settled in broad districts with ten years' tax and service exemption.

sentences.zh: 奴婢縱為良人，給復三年。

translations.literal: Slaves manumitted to commoner status received three years' remission.
translations.idiomatic: Freed slaves received three years' exemption from tax and corvée.

sentences.zh: 沒外蕃人，一年還者給復三年，二年者給復四年，三年者給復五年。

translations.literal: Foreigners lost beyond the frontier who returned within one year received three years' remission; within two years, four years; within three years, five years.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier peoples captured abroad who returned within one year received three years' exemption; within two years, four years; within three years, five years.

sentences.zh: 浮民、部曲、客女、奴婢縱為良者附寬鄉。

translations.literal: Vagrants, retainers, guest women, and slaves manumitted to commoner status were attached to broad districts.
translations.idiomatic: Vagrants, retainers, guest women, and freed slaves were registered in broad districts.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，初稅草以給諸閑，而驛馬有牧田。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era, a grass tax was first levied to supply various incidental needs, and relay horses had pasture fields.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan reign, a fodder tax was introduced for miscellaneous state needs, and post-station horses were given pasture land.

sentences.zh: 太宗方銳意於治，官吏考課，以鰥寡少者進考，如增戶法；

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong was then intent on good governance; in officials' performance reviews, those with few widowers and orphans advanced in assessment, as under the household-increase law;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong was then bent on good government; in performance reviews, officials were promoted for districts with few widowers and orphans, as under the household-growth statute;

sentences.zh: 失勸導者以減戶論。

translations.literal: those who failed in guidance were judged as having reduced households.
translations.idiomatic: and those who failed to encourage settlement were penalized as if they had lost population.

sentences.zh: 配租以斂穫早晚、險易、遠近為差。

translations.literal: Zu collection was apportioned with differences according to early or late harvest, difficulty or ease of terrain, and distance near or far.
translations.idiomatic: Grain tax collection was scheduled according to harvest timing, terrain, and distance.

sentences.zh: 庸、調輸以八月，發以九月。

translations.literal: Yong and diao were delivered in the eighth month and dispatched in the ninth.
translations.idiomatic: Corvée payments and textile taxes were due in the eighth month and forwarded in the ninth.

sentences.zh: 同時輸者先遠民。

translations.literal: When deliveries coincided, distant peoples were served first.
translations.idiomatic: When several districts paid at once, remoter districts went first.

sentences.zh: 皆自概量。

translations.literal: All were measured by the recipients themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Recipients measured the goods themselves.

sentences.zh: 州府歲市土所出為貢，其價視絹之上下，無過五十匹。

translations.literal: Prefectures and districts each year purchased local products as tribute; their value was gauged against higher or lower grades of silk, not exceeding fifty bolts.
translations.idiomatic: Each year prefectures purchased local products as tribute, valued against silk grades and capped at fifty bolts.

sentences.zh: 異物、滋味、口馬、鷹犬，非有詔不獻。

translations.literal: Rare goods, delicacies, horses for the mouth, hawks and hounds—without an edict they were not presented.
translations.idiomatic: Exotic goods, delicacies, riding horses, hawks, and hounds were not sent as tribute without imperial order.

sentences.zh: 有加配，則以代租賦。

translations.literal: If extra assignments were made, they substituted for zu and levies.
translations.idiomatic: Extra tribute assignments could be substituted for regular taxes.

sentences.zh: 其兇荒則有社倉賑給，不足則徙民就食諸州。

translations.literal: In famine and disaster there were community granaries for relief; if insufficient, the people were moved to other prefectures for food.
translations.idiomatic: In famine, community granaries provided relief; if stores ran short, people were relocated to other prefectures for food.

sentences.zh: 尚書左丞戴胄建議：「自王公以下，計墾田，秋熟，所在為義倉，歲兇以給民。

translations.literal: Left Vice Minister of the Secretariat Dai Zhou proposed: "From kings and dukes downward, reckon cultivated fields; when autumn ripens, establish charity granaries locally to supply the people in years of famine."
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Minister Dai Zhou proposed: "From princes and dukes down, tally cultivated land; after the autumn harvest, establish charity granaries in each locality to feed the people in bad years."

sentences.zh: 」太宗善之，乃詔：「畝稅二升，粟、麥、秔、稻，隨土地所宜。

translations.literal: " The Taizong emperor approved and issued an edict: "Two sheng tax per mu, of millet, wheat, japonica, or rice according to what the land suited."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong approved and decreed: "A levy of two sheng per mu, in millet, wheat, or rice as the soil allowed."

sentences.zh: 寬鄉斂以所種，狹鄉據青苗簿而督之。

translations.literal: In broad districts collection followed what was planted; in narrow districts it was enforced according to the green-crop register.
translations.idiomatic: Broad districts were taxed on what was actually planted; narrow districts were assessed from the green-crop register.

sentences.zh: 田耗十四者免其半，耗十七者皆免之。

translations.literal: Where fields lost fourteen parts in ten, half was remitted; where seventeen parts, all was remitted.
translations.idiomatic: A fourteen-tenths crop loss brought half remission; at seventeen-tenths, full remission.

sentences.zh: 商賈無田者，以其戶為九等，出粟自五石至於五斗為差。

translations.literal: Merchants without fields were ranked in nine grades by household, contributing grain from five shi down to five dou in graded amounts.
translations.idiomatic: Landless merchants were ranked in nine household grades, contributing from five shi down to five dou of grain.

sentences.zh: 下下戶及夷獠不取焉。

translations.literal: The lowest grade of households and Yi and Liao peoples were not levied.
translations.idiomatic: The poorest households and non-Han frontier peoples were exempt.

sentences.zh: 歲不登，則以賑民；

translations.literal: In years of poor harvest, grain was used to relieve the people;
translations.idiomatic: In lean years the grain was used for relief;

sentences.zh: 或貸為種子，則至秋而償。

translations.literal: or lent as seed, to be repaid by autumn.
translations.idiomatic: or lent as seed to be repaid after the autumn harvest.

sentences.zh: 」其後洛、相、幽、徐、齊、並、秦、蒲州又置常平倉，粟藏九年，米藏五年，下濕之地，粟藏五年，米藏三年，皆著於令。

translations.literal: " Later Luoyang, Xiang, You, Xu, Qi, Bing, Qin, and Pu prefectures also established Ever-Normal granaries: millet stored nine years, rice five; in damp lowlands, millet five years and rice three—all written into statute.
translations.idiomatic: Later Ever-Normal granaries were also set up in Luoyang, Xiangzhou, Youzhou, Xuzhou, Qizhou, Bingzhou, Qinzhou, and Puzhou: millet stored nine years and rice five, or in damp regions millet five years and rice three—all codified in law.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，戶不及三百萬，絹一匹易米一斗。

translations.literal: Early in Zhenguan, households did not reach three million; one bolt of silk exchanged for one dou of rice.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenguan era there were fewer than three million households, and one bolt of silk bought only one dou of rice.

sentences.zh: 至四年，米斗四五錢，外戶不閉者數月，馬牛被野，人行數千里不賫糧，民物蕃息，四夷降附者百二十萬人。

translations.literal: By the fourth year, one dou of rice cost four or five cash; outer gates were left unbarred for months; horses and cattle roamed the wilds; travelers went thousands of li without carrying grain; people and goods flourished; foreigners who submitted numbered 1.2 million.
translations.idiomatic: By the fourth year rice sold for four or five cash per dou; outer gates stood unbarred for months; horses and cattle grazed in the open fields; travelers went thousands of li without provisions; population and wealth prospered; and 1.2 million foreigners submitted.

sentences.zh: 是歲，天下斷獄，死罪者二十九人，號稱太平。

translations.literal: That year, capital cases throughout the realm numbered twenty-nine executions, and the age was called Great Peace.
translations.idiomatic: That year only twenty-nine people were executed for capital crimes empire-wide, and the reign was hailed as an age of great peace.

sentences.zh: 此高祖、太宗致治之大略，及其成效如此。

translations.literal: This was the great outline by which Gaozu and Taizong brought order, and their achievements were such as this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the broad fiscal policy by which Gaozu and Taizong brought order, and such were its results.

sentences.zh: 高宗承之，海內艾安。

translations.literal: Gaozong inherited it, and within the seas all was tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong inherited this order, and the realm remained at peace.

sentences.zh: 太尉長孫無忌等輔政，天下未見失德。

translations.literal: Grand Mentor Zhangsun Wuji and others assisted in government, and the realm saw no loss of virtue.
translations.idiomatic: With Zhangsun Wuji and others guiding policy, the court showed no serious lapse in governance.

sentences.zh: 數引刺史入閤，問民疾苦。

translations.literal: He repeatedly summoned prefectural governors into the palace to inquire about the people's hardships.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly summoned prefects to court to ask about the people's hardships.

sentences.zh: 即位之歲，增戶十五萬。

translations.literal: In the year of his accession, households increased by 150,000.
translations.idiomatic: In the year he took the throne, registered households rose by 150,000.

sentences.zh: 及中書令李義府、侍中許敬宗既用事，役費並起。

translations.literal: When Chief Minister Li Yifu and Palace Attendant Xu Jingzong came to power, corvée and expenditure rose together.
translations.idiomatic: Once Chief Minister Li Yifu and Palace Attendant Xu Jingzong gained power, labor levies and state spending both surged.

sentences.zh: 永淳以後，給用益不足。

translations.literal: After the Yongchun era, supplies and expenditure grew ever more insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yongchun era, revenue increasingly failed to meet expenses.

sentences.zh: 加以武後之亂，紀綱大壞，民不勝其毒。

translations.literal: Added to this was the turmoil of Empress Wu; institutions were greatly ruined and the people could not bear the poison.
translations.idiomatic: Then came the chaos of Empress Wu's reign; government collapsed and the people could not endure the oppression.

sentences.zh: 玄宗初立求治，蠲徭役者給蠲符，以流外及九品京官為蠲使，歲再遣之。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong first took the throne seeking good governance, those remitted from corvée were given remission tallies; officials outside the regular roster and capital officials of ninth rank served as remission envoys, dispatched twice yearly.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong first sought to restore good government, those exempted from corvée received exemption certificates; junior capital officials served as exemption commissioners and were sent out twice a year.

sentences.zh: 開元八年，頒庸調法於天下，好不過精，惡不至濫，闊者一尺八寸，長者四丈。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Kaiyuan, the yong and diao law was promulgated throughout the realm: fine goods must not exceed standard quality, poor goods must not fall to shoddy grade; width at least one chi eight cun, length at most four zhang.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 8 the corvée and textile tax standards were issued empire-wide: top quality could not exceed the fine grade, poor quality could not fall below the lowest acceptable grade; width at least one chi eight cun and length no more than four zhang.

sentences.zh: 然是時天下戶未嘗升降。

translations.literal: Yet at this time household registers throughout the realm had never been raised or lowered.
translations.idiomatic: Yet household registers empire-wide had never been properly updated.

sentences.zh: 監察御史宇文融獻策：括籍外羨田、逃戶，自占者給復五年，每丁稅錢千五百，以攝御史分行括實。

translations.literal: Investigating Censor Yuwen Rong submitted a plan: register surplus fields outside the rolls and fugitive households; those who reported themselves received five years' remission; each ding paid 1,500 cash in tax; acting censors were sent in branches to verify registration.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating Censor Yuwen Rong proposed registering unreported surplus land and fugitive households: self-reporting households received five years' exemption and paid 1,500 cash per adult male; acting censors were dispatched to verify the rolls.

sentences.zh: 陽翟尉皇甫憬上書言其不可。

translations.literal: Yangdi District Assistant Huangfu Jing memorialized that this could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Yangdi District Assistant Huangfu Jing submitted a memorial arguing against the plan.

sentences.zh: 玄宗方任用融，乃貶憬為盈川尉。

translations.literal: Xuanzong was then employing Rong and demoted Jing to district assistant of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong, then relying on Rong, demoted Jing to assistant magistrate of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 諸道所括得客戶八十余萬，田亦稱是。

translations.literal: The various circuits registered more than 800,000 client households, and fields in like measure.
translations.idiomatic: The circuits registered more than 800,000 client households and a corresponding amount of land.

sentences.zh: 州縣希旨張虛數，以正田為羨，編戶為客，歲終，籍錢數百萬緡。

translations.literal: Prefectures and districts, eager to please, inflated false figures, treating regular fields as surplus and registered households as client households; by year's end they registered several million strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures and districts, eager to please, inflated the rolls—reporting regular fields as surplus land and registered households as client households—and by year's end had logged several million strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 十六年，乃詔每三歲以九等定籍。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, an edict ordered household registers fixed by nine grades every three years.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year an edict required household registers to be ranked in nine grades every three years.

sentences.zh: 而庸調折租所取華好，州縣長宮勸織，中書門下察濫惡以貶官吏，精者褒賞之。

translations.literal: For yong, diao, and converted zu collections, only fine goods were taken; prefectural and district chiefs urged weaving; the Secretariat and Chancellery inspected shoddy goods to demote officials, and rewarded the finest.
translations.idiomatic: Corvée payments, textile taxes, and grain-tax conversions had to be of the finest quality; local officials urged weaving; the Secretariat inspected inferior goods and demoted officials, while rewarding excellence.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，詔男十五、女十三以上得嫁娶。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, an edict allowed men of fifteen and women of thirteen and above to marry.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year an edict permitted marriage for men of fifteen and women of thirteen and above.

sentences.zh: 州縣歲上戶口登耗，采訪使覆實之，刺史、縣令以為課最。

translations.literal: Each year prefectures and districts reported household increases and losses; investigating commissioners verified them, and prefects and magistrates were judged on this as their chief performance measure.
translations.idiomatic: Each year prefectures reported household gains and losses; investigating commissioners verified the figures, and prefects and magistrates were chiefly judged on this performance.

sentences.zh: 初，永徽中禁買賣世業、口分田。

translations.literal: At first, in the Yonghui era, sale of hereditary estate and per-capita allotment fields was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, during the Yonghui era, the sale of permanent holdings and per-capita allotments was forbidden.

sentences.zh: 其後豪富兼並，貧者失業，於是詔買者還地而罰之。

translations.literal: Afterward the wealthy consolidated holdings and the poor lost their livelihoods, whereupon an edict ordered buyers to return the land and imposed penalties.
translations.idiomatic: Later the rich consolidated land and the poor lost their livelihoods, so an edict required buyers to return the land and imposed penalties.

sentences.zh: 先是楊州租、調以錢，嶺南以米，安南以絲，益州以羅、䌷、綾、絹供春彩。

translations.literal: Previously Yangzhou paid zu and diao in cash, Lingnan in rice, Annan in silk, and Yizhou supplied gauze, crepe, damask, and silk for spring tribute fabrics.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yangzhou paid grain and textile taxes in cash, Lingnan in rice, Annan in silk, and Yizhou supplied gauze, crepe, damask, and silk for spring tribute cloth.

sentences.zh: 因詔江南亦以布代租。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered south of the Yangzi also to substitute cloth for zu.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then allowed south of the Yangzi to pay the grain tax in cloth instead.

sentences.zh: 中書令李林甫以租庸、丁防、和糴、春彩、稅草無定法，歲為旨符，遣使一告，費紙五十余萬。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Li Linfu, because zu, yong, corvée garrisons, government grain purchases, spring fabrics, and grass taxes had no fixed law and yearly edict tallies were sent by a single messenger's announcement, consumed more than five hundred thousand sheets of paper.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Li Linfu noted that grain tax, corvée, garrison service, government grain purchases, spring tribute cloth, and fodder tax had no fixed rules; each year edict tallies were sent out by messenger at a cost of more than five hundred thousand sheets of paper.

sentences.zh: 條目既多，覆問逾年，乃與采訪朝集使議革之，為長行旨，以授朝集使及送旨符使，歲有所支，進畫附驛以達，每州不過二紙。

translations.literal: The entries being numerous, replies took more than a year; he then discussed reform with investigating and assembly commissioners, making standing edict provisions to give to assembly commissioners and edict-delivery envoys; yearly expenditures were listed, submitted in sealed packets via post relay, and each prefecture received no more than two sheets.
translations.idiomatic: With so many entries, verification took more than a year; he then worked with investigating and assembly commissioners to reform the system into standing regulations for assembly commissioners and edict couriers; annual expenditures were listed, sent by sealed relay post, with no more than two sheets per prefecture.

sentences.zh: 凡庸、調、租、資課，皆任土所宜，州縣長官涖定粗良，具上中下三物之樣輸京都。

translations.literal: For yong, diao, zu, and resource levies generally, local products were used as suited; prefectural and district chiefs personally fixed coarse and fine grades and submitted samples of upper, middle, and lower goods to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Corvée, textile, grain, and resource levies all followed local products; prefectural and district chiefs set coarse and fine grades and sent samples of upper, middle, and lower quality to the capital.

sentences.zh: 有濫惡，督中物之直。

translations.literal: If goods were shoddy, the price of middle-grade goods was exacted.
translations.idiomatic: Shoddy goods were charged at middle-grade prices.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，以江、淮輸運有河、洛之艱，而關中蠶桑少，菽粟常賤，乃命庸、調、資課皆以米，兇年樂輸布絹者亦從之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, because transport from the Jiang and Huai faced the hardships of the Yellow and Luo routes, while Guanzhong had little sericulture and legumes and grain were always cheap, yong, diao, and resource levies were all ordered paid in rice; in famine years those willing to pay in cloth and silk were also allowed to do so.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year, because shipping from the Jiang-Huai region faced the difficulties of the Yellow and Luo routes while Guanzhong had little sericulture and grain was cheap, corvée, textile, and resource levies were ordered paid in rice; in famine years those willing to pay in cloth and silk were also permitted.

sentences.zh: 河南、北不通運州，租皆為絹，代關中庸、課，詔度支減轉運。

translations.literal: In Henan and Hebei, prefectures without transport access paid zu entirely in silk, substituting for Guanzhong yong and levies; the Department of Public Works was ordered to reduce transport.
translations.idiomatic: In Henan and Hebei, prefectures without transport links paid the grain tax entirely in silk to substitute for Guanzhong corvée and levies, and the expenditure office was ordered to cut transport costs.

sentences.zh: 明年，又詔民三歲以下為黃，十五以下為小，二十以下為中。

translations.literal: The next year, another edict classified people under three as huang, under fifteen as xiao, and under twenty as zhong.
translations.idiomatic: The next year another edict classified those under three as infants, under fifteen as children, and under twenty as youths.

sentences.zh: 又以民間戶高丁多者，率與父母別籍異居，以避征戍，乃詔十丁以上免二丁，五丁以上免一丁，侍丁孝者免徭役。

translations.literal: Moreover, because wealthy households with many adult males commonly separated registers and lived apart from parents to avoid conscription, an edict exempted two ding from households of ten or more and one ding from households of five or more; filial attendants were exempt from corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Because wealthy households with many adult sons commonly split registers and lived apart from parents to avoid conscription, an edict exempted two adult males from households of ten or more and one from households of five or more; filial attendants were exempt from corvée.

sentences.zh: 天寶三載，更民十八以上為中男，二十三以上成丁。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianbao, males eighteen and above were reclassified as zhongnan, and twenty-three and above as ding.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 3 males of eighteen and above were reclassified as youths, and those of twenty-three and above as adult males liable for service.

sentences.zh: 五載，詔貧不能自濟者，每鄉免三十丁租庸。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, an edict remitted zu and yong for thirty ding per district among those too poor to support themselves.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year an edict exempted thirty adult males per district from grain tax and corvée among those too poor to support themselves.

sentences.zh: 男子七十五以上、婦人七十以上，中男一人為侍；

translations.literal: Men seventy-five and above and women seventy and above were granted one zhongnan as attendant;
translations.idiomatic: Men seventy-five and above and women seventy and above were granted one youth as attendant;

sentences.zh: 八十以上以令式從事。

translations.literal: those eighty and above were treated according to statutes and regulations.
translations.idiomatic: those eighty and above were treated according to statute.

sentences.zh: 是時，海內富實，米鬥之價錢十三，青、齊間鬥才三錢，絹一匹錢二百。

translations.literal: At this time the realm was rich and solid: a dou of rice cost thirteen cash; between Qing and Qi only three cash per dou; one bolt of silk two hundred cash.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the realm was prosperous: rice sold for thirteen cash per dou, only three cash in Qing and Qi, and two hundred cash per bolt of silk.

sentences.zh: 道路列肆，具酒食以待行人，店有驛驢，行千里不持尺兵。

translations.literal: Shops lined the roads with wine and food awaiting travelers; inns had relay donkeys; one traveled a thousand li without carrying a weapon.
translations.idiomatic: Shops lined the roads with wine and food for travelers; inns kept relay donkeys; one could travel a thousand li unarmed.

sentences.zh: 天下歲入之物，租錢二百余萬緡，粟千九百八十余萬斛，庸、調絹七百四十萬匹，綿百八十余萬屯，布千三十五萬余端。

translations.literal: The realm's yearly intake was: zu in cash more than two million strings; grain more than 19.8 million hu; yong and diao silk 7.4 million bolts; cotton more than 1.8 million tun; cloth more than 10.35 million duan.
translations.idiomatic: Annual revenue empire-wide included more than two million strings in grain-tax cash, more than 19.8 million hu of grain, 7.4 million bolts of silk for corvée and textile taxes, more than 1.8 million bales of cotton, and more than 10.35 million bolts of cloth.

sentences.zh: 天子驕於佚樂而用不知節，大抵用物之數，常過其所入。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven grew arrogant in idle pleasure and did not know restraint in expenditure; generally the quantity of goods used always exceeded intake.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew arrogant in pleasure and knew no restraint in spending; consumption routinely exceeded revenue.

sentences.zh: 於是錢谷之臣，始事朘刻。

translations.literal: Thereupon ministers of revenue began to practice squeezing and exacting.
translations.idiomatic: Revenue officials then began to practice extortion and petty exaction.

sentences.zh: 太府卿楊崇禮句剝分銖，有欠折漬損者，州縣督送，歷年不止。

translations.literal: Grand Treasury Director Yang Chongli scraped and split every fen and zhu; where there were shortages, spoilage, or damage, prefectures and districts were compelled to make delivery, year after year without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Treasury Director Yang Chongli wrung out every penny; shortages, spoilage, or damage were chased down by prefectures and districts year after year without end.

sentences.zh: 其子慎矜專知太府，次子慎名知京倉，亦以苛刻結主恩。

translations.literal: His son Shenjin exclusively managed the Grand Treasury; his second son Shenming managed the capital granaries; both also won imperial favor through harshness.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shenjin ran the Grand Treasury and his second son Shenming the capital granaries; both also curried favor through harsh exaction.

sentences.zh: 王鉷為戶口色役使，歲進錢百億萬緡，非租庸正額者，積百寶大盈庫，以供天子燕私。

translations.literal: Wang Hong served as commissioner for household registers and corvée categories, annually presenting ten billion strings of cash; amounts outside the regular zu and yong quotas were stored in the Great Abundance Treasury of accumulated treasures to supply the Son of Heaven's private pleasures.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hong served as commissioner for household registers and corvée categories, annually presenting ten billion strings; sums outside regular grain and corvée quotas went to the Great Abundance Treasury for the emperor's private use.

sentences.zh: 及安祿山反，司空楊國忠以為正庫物不可以給士，遣侍御史崔眾至太原納錢度僧尼道士，旬日得百萬緡而已。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, Minister of Works Yang Guozhong held that regular treasury goods could not supply the troops; he sent Attending Censor Cui Zhong to Taiyuan to collect cash for ordaining Buddhist monks and Daoist priests; in ten days only one million strings were obtained.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, Minister of Works Yang Guozhong argued that regular treasury goods could not supply the army; he sent Attending Censor Cui Zhong to Taiyuan to collect cash by ordaining monks and priests, raising only one million strings in ten days.

sentences.zh: 自兩京陷沒，民物耗弊，天下蕭然。

translations.literal: From the fall of the two capitals, people and goods were depleted and ruined; the realm was desolate.
translations.idiomatic: After the two capitals fell, people and goods were devastated and the realm lay in ruin.

sentences.zh: 肅宗即位，遣御史鄭叔清等籍江淮、蜀漢富商右族訾畜，十收其二，謂之率貸。

translations.literal: When Suzong took the throne, he sent Censor Zheng Shuqing and others to register the assets of wealthy merchants and great clans of the Jiang-Huai, Shu, and Han regions, taking two parts in ten—called "assessed lending."
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong took the throne, he sent Censor Zheng Shuqing and others to register the assets of wealthy merchants and great families in the Jiang-Huai, Shu, and Han regions, taking two-tenths—a levy called "assessed lending."

sentences.zh: 諸道亦稅商賈以贍軍，錢一千者有稅。

translations.literal: The various circuits also taxed merchants to support the army; for every thousand cash there was a tax.
translations.idiomatic: The circuits also taxed merchants to support the army, levying on every thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 於是北海郡錄事參軍第五琦以錢谷得見，請於江淮置租庸使，吳鹽、蜀麻、銅冶皆有稅，市輕貨繇江陵、襄陽、上津路轉至鳳翔。

translations.literal: Thereupon Beihai District Recorder Diwu Qi gained audience through revenue expertise and requested establishing zu-yong commissioners in the Jiang-Huai; Wu salt, Shu hemp, and copper smelting were all taxed; light goods were marketed and transported via Jiangling, Xiangyang, and the Shangjin route to Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Beihai District Recorder Diwu Qi then gained audience through fiscal expertise and proposed zu-yong commissioners in the Jiang-Huai; Wu salt, Shu hemp, and copper smelting were taxed; light goods were shipped via Jiangling, Xiangyang, and the Shangjin route to Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 明年，鄭叔清與宰相裴冕建議，以天下用度不充，諸道得召人納錢，給空名告身，授官勛邑號；

translations.literal: The next year Zheng Shuqing and Chief Minister Pei Mian proposed that because empire-wide expenditure was insufficient, circuits might summon people to pay cash and receive blank commission credentials, granting offices, merit titles, and fief designations;
translations.idiomatic: The next year Zheng Shuqing and Chief Minister Pei Mian proposed that because state revenue was insufficient, circuits could accept cash for blank commission credentials granting offices, merit titles, and fief names;

sentences.zh: 度道士僧尼不可勝計；

translations.literal: ordained Daoist priests and Buddhist monks and nuns beyond counting;
translations.idiomatic: ordained Daoist priests and Buddhist monks and nuns beyond counting;

sentences.zh: 納錢百千，賜明經出身；

translations.literal: those paying a hundred thousand cash were granted mingjing examination status;
translations.idiomatic: those paying a hundred thousand cash received mingjing examination credentials;

sentences.zh: 商賈助軍者，給復。

translations.literal: merchants who aided the army received remission of tax and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: merchants who aided the army received tax and service exemption.

sentences.zh: 及兩京平，又於關輔諸州，納錢度道士僧尼萬人。

translations.literal: When the two capitals were recovered, in the Guanfu prefectures ten thousand Daoist priests and Buddhist monks and nuns were ordained for cash.
translations.idiomatic: When the two capitals were recovered, ten thousand monks and priests were ordained for cash in the Guanfu prefectures.

sentences.zh: 而百姓殘於兵盜，米鬥至錢七千，鬻籺為糧，民行乞食者屬路。

translations.literal: Yet the people were ravaged by war and bandits; a dou of rice reached seven thousand cash; chaff was sold as grain; beggars lined the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the people were ravaged by war and banditry; rice reached seven thousand cash per dou; chaff was sold as grain; and beggars lined the roads.

sentences.zh: 乃詔能賑貧乏者，寵以爵衤失。

translations.literal: An edict then honored those who could relieve the poor with titles and robes of rank.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then honored those who relieved the poor with titles and robes of rank.

sentences.zh: 故事，天下財賦歸左藏，而太府以時上其數，尚書比部覆其出入。

translations.literal: By precedent, empire-wide revenue went to the Left Vault, while the Grand Treasury reported its figures on schedule and the Ministry of Revenue's Comparison Section audited receipts and disbursements.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent empire-wide revenue went to the Left Vault; the Grand Treasury reported figures on schedule and the Ministry of Revenue audited receipts and disbursements.

sentences.zh: 是時，京師豪將假取不能禁，第五琦為度支鹽鐵使，請皆歸大盈庫，供天子給賜，主以中官。

translations.literal: At this time capital military grandees borrowed funds without restraint; Diwu Qi as salt and iron commissioner of the expenditure office requested that all revenue go to the Great Abundance Treasury to supply the Son of Heaven's gifts and grants, managed by palace eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: Capital military grandees then borrowed funds without restraint; Diwu Qi as expenditure and salt commissioner proposed that all revenue go to the Great Abundance Treasury for imperial gifts, managed by palace eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 自是天下之財為人君私藏，有司不得程其多少。

translations.literal: From this the realm's wealth became the ruler's private store; officials could not reckon its amount.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the realm's wealth became the emperor's private hoard, beyond official accounting.

sentences.zh: 廣德元年，詔一戶三丁者免一丁，凡畝稅二升，男子二十五為成丁，五十五為老，以優民。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangde, an edict exempted one ding from households of three ding; generally two sheng tax per mu; men twenty-five became ding, fifty-five became lao—to benefit the people.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangde 1 an edict exempted one adult male from households of three; set a general levy of two sheng per mu; made twenty-five the age of full liability and fifty-five the age of elder exemption—to ease the people's burden.

sentences.zh: 而強寇未夷，民耗斂重。

translations.literal: Yet powerful bandits were not pacified and the people's losses from levies were heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Yet powerful rebels were not pacified and levies still weighed heavily on the people.

sentences.zh: 及吐蕃逼京師，近甸屯兵數萬，百官進俸錢，又率戶以給軍糧。

translations.literal: When Tibetans pressed the capital, tens of thousands of troops were garrisoned in nearby districts; officials contributed salary funds and households were levied for army grain.
translations.idiomatic: When Tibetans threatened the capital, tens of thousands of troops were garrisoned nearby; officials contributed salary funds and households were levied for army grain.

sentences.zh: 至大歷元年，詔流民還者，給復二年，田園盡，則授以逃田。

translations.literal: By the first year of Dali, an edict gave returning refugees two years' remission; if fields and gardens were gone, abandoned fields were granted.
translations.idiomatic: By Dali 1 returning refugees received two years' exemption; if their land was gone, abandoned fields were granted.

sentences.zh: 天下苗一畝稅錢十五，市輕貨給百官手力課。

translations.literal: Empire-wide, fifteen cash tax per mu on seedlings; light goods were marketed to supply officials' labor-service levies.
translations.idiomatic: Empire-wide a seedling tax of fifteen cash per mu was levied; light goods were sold to fund officials' labor allowances.

sentences.zh: 以國用急，不及秋，方苗青即征之，號「青苗錢」又有「地頭錢」，每畝二十，通名為青苗錢。

translations.literal: Because state needs were urgent, before autumn while seedlings were still green they were levied—called "green-crop money"; there was also "field-head money" of twenty per mu; both were commonly called green-crop money.
translations.idiomatic: Because revenue was urgent, tax was collected while seedlings were still green before autumn—called "green-crop money"; there was also "field-head money" of twenty per mu; both were known as green-crop money.

sentences.zh: 又詔上都秋稅分二等，上等畝稅一斗，下等六升，荒田畝稅二升。

translations.literal: Another edict divided the upper capital's autumn tax into two grades: upper fields one dou per mu, lower fields six sheng, wasteland two sheng per mu.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict divided the capital's autumn tax into two grades: upper fields one dou per mu, lower six sheng, wasteland two sheng.

sentences.zh: 五年，始定法：夏，上田畝稅六升，下田畝四升；

translations.literal: In the fifth year the law was first fixed: in summer, upper fields six sheng per mu, lower fields four sheng;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the law was fixed: in summer, upper fields six sheng per mu, lower fields four;

sentences.zh: 秋，上田畝稅五升，下田畝三升；

translations.literal: in autumn, upper fields five sheng per mu, lower fields three sheng;
translations.idiomatic: in autumn, upper fields five sheng per mu, lower three;

sentences.zh: 荒田如故；

translations.literal: wasteland as before;
translations.idiomatic: wasteland as before;

sentences.zh: 青苗錢畝加一倍，而地頭錢不在焉。

translations.literal: green-crop money was doubled per mu, but field-head money was not included.
translations.idiomatic: green-crop money was doubled per mu, but field-head money was excluded.

sentences.zh: 初，轉運使掌外，度支使掌內。

translations.literal: At first the transport commissioner managed external revenue and the expenditure commissioner managed internal.
translations.idiomatic: Initially the transport commissioner managed external revenue and the expenditure commissioner internal revenue.

sentences.zh: 永泰二年，分天下財賦、鑄錢、常平、轉運、鹽鐵，置二使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongtai, empire-wide revenue, coinage, Ever-Normal granaries, transport, and salt and iron were divided and two commissioners were established.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongtai 2 empire-wide revenue, coinage, Ever-Normal granaries, transport, and salt and iron were split between two commissioners.

sentences.zh: 東都畿內、河南、淮南、江東西、湖南、荊南、山南東道，以轉運使劉晏領之；

translations.literal: The Eastern Capital metropolitan region, Henan, Huainan, Jiangdong and Jiangxi, Hunan, Jingnan, and Shannan East Circuit were led by Transport Commissioner Liu Yan;
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Capital region, Henan, Huainan, Jiangdong and Jiangxi, Hunan, Jingnan, and Shannan East were assigned to Transport Commissioner Liu Yan;

sentences.zh: 京畿、關內、河東、劍南、山南西道，以京兆尹、判度支第五琦領之。

translations.literal: the Capital Metropolitan, Guannei, Hedong, Jiannan, and Shannan West circuits were led by the Jingzhao governor and acting expenditure commissioner Diwu Qi.
translations.idiomatic: the Capital Metropolitan, Guannei, Hedong, Jiannan, and Shannan West circuits to Jingzhao Governor and acting expenditure commissioner Diwu Qi.

sentences.zh: 及琦貶，以戶部侍郎、判度支韓滉與晏分治。

translations.literal: When Qi was demoted, Vice Minister of Revenue and acting expenditure commissioner Han Huang shared administration with Yan.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi was demoted, Vice Minister of Revenue and acting expenditure commissioner Han Huang shared administration with Yan.

sentences.zh: 時回紇有助收西京功，代宗厚遇之，與中國婚姻，歲送馬十萬匹，酬以縑帛百余萬匹。

translations.literal: At this time the Uyghurs had aided in recovering the Western Capital; Daizong treated them generously, intermarried with China, and each year sent one hundred thousand horses, repaid with more than a million bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs had helped recover the Western Capital; Daizong treated them generously, intermarried with them, and each year sent one hundred thousand horses, repaid with more than a million bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 而中國財力屈竭，歲負馬價。

translations.literal: Yet China's financial strength was exhausted and each year owed for the horses.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the empire's finances were exhausted and each year fell short of the horse payments.

sentences.zh: 河、湟六鎮既陷，歲發防秋兵三萬戍京西，資糧百五十余萬緡。

translations.literal: After the six Hehuang garrisons fell, each year thirty thousand autumn-defense troops were sent to garrison western Jing, costing more than 1.5 million strings in provisions.
translations.idiomatic: After the six Hehuang garrisons fell, thirty thousand autumn-defense troops were sent yearly to garrison western Jing at a cost of more than 1.5 million strings in provisions.

sentences.zh: 而中官魚朝恩方恃恩擅權，代宗與宰相元載日夜圖之。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the eunuch Yu Chaoen relied on favor and monopolized power; Daizong and Chief Minister Yuan Zai plotted against him day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the eunuch Yu Chaoen monopolized power through imperial favor; Daizong and Chief Minister Yuan Zai plotted against him day and night.

sentences.zh: 及朝恩誅，帝復與載貳，君臣猜間不協，邊計兵食，置而不議者幾十年。

translations.literal: After Chaoen was executed, the emperor again grew estranged from Zai; ruler and minister were suspicious and at odds; frontier plans and army provisions went undiscussed for nearly ten years.
translations.idiomatic: After Chaoen was executed, the emperor again turned against Zai; ruler and minister grew suspicious and estranged; frontier strategy and army provisions went undiscussed for nearly ten years.

sentences.zh: 而諸鎮擅地，結為表裏，日治兵繕壘，天子不能繩以法，顓留意祠禱、焚幣玉、寫浮屠書，度支稟賜僧巫，歲以鉅萬計。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the military governors seized territory and acted in concert inside and out, daily drilling troops and repairing ramparts; the Son of Heaven could not restrain them by law and devoted himself solely to temple prayers, burning jade and silk offerings, and copying Buddhist sutras; the expenditure office supplied monks and shamans by the tens of thousands each year.
translations.idiomatic: Military governors seized territory and acted in concert, daily drilling troops and repairing fortifications; the emperor could not restrain them by law and devoted himself to temple prayers, burning jade offerings, and copying Buddhist sutras; the expenditure office supplied monks and shamans at a cost of tens of thousands each year.

sentences.zh: 然帝性儉約，身所禦衣，必浣染至再三，欲以先天下。

translations.literal: Yet the emperor's nature was frugal; the robes he wore were washed and dyed again and again, wishing to take the lead for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the emperor was personally frugal; he wore his robes washed and dyed again and again, hoping to set an example for the realm.

sentences.zh: 然生日、端午，四方貢獻至數千萬者，加以恩澤，而諸道尚侈麗以自媚。

translations.literal: Yet on his birthday and the Dragon Boat Festival, tribute from the four quarters reached tens of millions; added to his largesse, the circuits still favored extravagant splendor to flatter themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Yet on his birthday and the Dragon Boat Festival tribute from the provinces reached tens of millions; combined with his largesse, the circuits still competed in extravagant display to curry favor.

sentences.zh: 朝多留事，經歲不能遣，置客省以居，上封事不足采者、蕃夷貢獻未報及失職未敘者，食度支數千百人。

translations.literal: The court retained many matters unresolved for years without dispatch; a Guest Reception Office was established to house them—memorials not worth adopting, foreign tribute unanswered, and dismissed officials not yet reassigned—feeding thousands on the expenditure office.
translations.idiomatic: The court left many matters unresolved for years; a Guest Reception Office housed rejected memorials, unanswered foreign tribute, and officials awaiting reassignment—thousands fed at state expense.

sentences.zh: 德宗即位，用宰相崔祐甫，拘客省者出之，食度支者遣之，歲省費萬計。

translations.literal: When Dezong took the throne, he employed Chief Minister Cui Youfu, released those detained in the Guest Reception Office, dismissed those fed by the expenditure office, and saved tens of thousands in yearly costs.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong took the throne, he employed Chief Minister Cui Youfu, released those detained in the Guest Reception Office, dismissed those on state stipends, and saved tens of thousands in annual costs.
